seoTitle: Free llms.txt Generator for AI Assistants
metaDescription: Create an llms.txt file that lists your key pages with short descriptions for AI assistants. Free; built in your browser.
intro: Write a title, summary and sections of links, and get a correctly formatted llms.txt file: a markdown index of your most useful pages for AI assistants to read.
why:
The llms.txt idea is a plain markdown file at the root of a site that tells AI assistants what the site is and which pages matter most, in a form that is easy to read without crawling the whole site. It is a proposal and not a standard, and no search engine or AI company guarantees that it will read it.

This generator saves you the formatting. Enter a title, a one-line summary and optional details, then sections with lines of name, URL and a short description. It outputs the heading, the quote block summary and a list of links under each section heading. A section called Optional marks lower-priority pages. Save the result as llms.txt in your site root. Nothing is sent anywhere, because the file is produced in your browser.
howTo: Fill in title, summary and details at the top of the box.
Add sections with a line starting ## and then one link per line in the form name | url | description.
Run the tool to produce the formatted file.
Save the result as llms.txt and place it at the root of your site.

faq.q: Do AI assistants actually use llms.txt?
faq.a: There is no guarantee. It is a community proposal, and support varies between tools. It costs little to add, but do not expect a measurable effect on search or AI answers.

faq.q: What does the Optional section mean?
faq.a: In the proposal, a section named Optional lists secondary links that can be skipped when a short context is needed. Put background material there and your essentials in the main sections.

faq.q: What is the link line format?
faq.a: Use name | url | description, with the description optional. The tool writes it as a markdown list item with the name linked to the URL, followed by a colon and the description.

faq.q: Is my content sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The calculation runs in your browser and nothing you paste is uploaded, stored or sent to a server, so drafts and confidential copy are safe to check.
